where: Section 3, definition of modulation index m
problem: The phrase 'peak swing of the optical power divided by its mean value' can be read as the full peak-to-peak swing, which would make m twice as large as intended. The rest of the chapter (signal current mI/√2, signal power (mI)²/2) assumes m is the peak deviation from the mean, so a student who reads 'peak swing' as peak-to-peak will get the wrong formula.
fix: Say: 'The modulation index m, no unit, is the peak deviation of the optical power from its mean divided by that mean value, that is m = (P_max − P_min)/(P_max + P_min). With P(t) = P₀(1 + m cos ωt), the peak deviation is mP₀ and the mean is P₀.'

problem: 'CNR = 6.125 ÷ 2.5 × 10⁻⁵' reads left to right as 6.125 ÷ 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ = 2.45 × 10⁻⁵ under normal precedence, which contradicts the stated answer 2.45 × 10⁵. The10⁻⁵ belongs in the denominator.
